evals.prompt: Group the issues labelled high into sets I can each work on in a single PR.
evals.expected_output: Cohesive groups with files named, a merge order, and a parallelism verdict. #1 and #2 must be one group (both live in iosApp/KaappiStudio/Resources/webview/bridge.js and form one silent-failure chain). #3, #9 and #11 must respect the dependency edges stated in their bodies (#3 and #11 lean on #9's per-run isolation). #5 must be identified as land-first because it makes verification untrustworthy (signal-before-work).
expectations: #1 and #2 appear in the same group, justified by both living in iosApp/KaappiStudio/Resources/webview/bridge.js
#5 is ordered before the groups it unblocks, on signal-before-work grounds (a failing Android Run does not disprove a fix while #5 stands)
The dependency edges from issue bodies (#3 → #9, #11 → #9, #4 → #14) are applied as hard ordering edges
Every group names the files it touches, and webview groups say which copy of the assets they touch
An explicit merge order is given, marking which groups are parallel

evals.prompt: Batch the issues labelled medium into single-PR sets.
evals.expected_output: Groups as above, plus #8 grouped as one root cause (unsanitized filenames plus swallowed write errors) spanning the Android FileRepository actual and the Swift FileBrowserViewModel, and #13 identified as land-first signal (iOS CI executes zero tests, so every iOS PR is green for free).
expectations: #8 groups the Android and iOS filename failures as one shared cause stated in a sentence, not as two platform-labeled issues
#13 is ordered early on signal-before-work grounds
The response does not group #6 and #7 merely because both carry the webview label (different mechanisms, different files)
#4 is marked design-first or split, because its durable fix is hostage to #14's framework decision
The long pole is named, with a statement of whether the rest ships without it

evals.prompt: Group the open issues labelled wontfix into PRs.
evals.expected_output: A statement that no open issues carry that label, and no groups — must not fall back to the whole tracker.
expectations: Response states that the label matched no open issues
Response contains no groups
Response does not fall back to grouping all open issues

evals.prompt: Which of these can I do in one PR: 1, 2? (skill argument: 1,2)
evals.expected_output: One group containing both, justified as the same file and one silent-failure chain in the iOS bridge — the broken fetch(file://) load (#1) and the missing runError plumbing that hides every failure (#2) must land together or the fix is still invisible.
expectations: Both issues are placed in a single group
The group names iosApp/KaappiStudio/Resources/webview/bridge.js with the relevant lines
The response states that the Android copy of bridge.js is intentionally different, so no mirrored edit is needed there
The response notes the fix should include posting runError from the init-failure and runCode-guard paths (#2's second half)

evals.prompt: I want to launch concurrent sessions on the high-severity fixes rather than review a plan — give me the waves.
evals.expected_output: Bare paste-able wave lines containing only issue numbers, with every group in a wave touching files no other group in that wave touches.
expectations: Response contains 'Wave N:' lines with comma-separated issue numbers
No issue number appears in more than one wave
Groups sharing a file never appear in the same wave
The wave lines contain no prose or commands mixed in

evals.prompt: Start wave 1 sessions for the plan you just gave me.
evals.expected_output: One session per wave-1 group launched concurrently, each in its own git worktree on a branch off a freshly-fetched origin/main, with a self-contained brief and the wrap-up contract (unit tests extended per the AGENTS.md test layout, short imperative commit subject, per-issue Closes keyword, gh pr create).
expectations: Each group is launched in its own git worktree, never in the shared checkout or on main
Branches are cut from a freshly-fetched origin/main (git fetch first), not from the possibly-stale local checkout
All groups of the wave are launched concurrently rather than one at a time
Each session brief is self-contained and tells the session to read the issue bodies itself

The wrap-up contract states: extend/adjust unit tests (commonTest via :shared:testAndroidHostTest, app/src/test via ./gradlew test), short imperative commit subject, no version-bump commits, push, gh pr create with a per-issue Closes line
Gradle checks are directed to run in the foreground as one blocking call, not backgrounded waiting on a notification
The response warns that concurrent Gradle builds serialize on the project lock and that a waiting build is not hung
The response does not treat a single worktree's green test run as proof that main is green
